questions.q:
The point A is (−2, 3).
(a) Write down the coordinates of the image of A after a reflection in the x-axis. [1]
(b) Write down the coordinates of the image of A after a translation by the vector (5 over −1). [1]
questions.model:
(a) Reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate: (−2, −3).
(b) (−2 + 5, 3 − 1) = (3, 2).
questions.tip: The top number of a column vector moves you horizontally, the bottom number vertically.

questions.q:
Triangle P has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 2).
Triangle Q has vertices (1, −1), (3, −1) and (1, −2).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle P onto triangle Q.
questions.model: Reflection in the x-axis (the line y = 0).
questions.tip: 'Reflected in the x-axis' needs both the word reflection and the mirror line.

questions.q:
Triangle A has vertices (2, 1), (4, 1) and (4, 4).
(a) Triangle A is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the point (1, 0). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image. [2]
(b) Triangle A is enlarged by scale factor ½, centre (0, 1). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image. [2]
ms: (a) B1: two correct vertices, or a correct 90° anticlockwise rotation about a different centre
questions.model:
(a) Relative to (1, 0) the vertices are (1, 1), (3, 1), (3, 4).
Rotating 90° anticlockwise: (x, y) → (−y, x) gives (−1, 1), (−1, 3), (−4, 3).
Add the centre back: (0, 1), (0, 3), (−3, 3).
(b) Relative to (0, 1): (2, 0), (4, 0), (4, 3). Halve: (1, 0), (2, 0), (2, 1.5).
Add the centre back: (1, 1), (2, 1), (2, 2.5).
questions.tip: Work relative to the centre: subtract it, transform, then add it back.

questions.q:
Triangle P has vertices (2, 2), (4, 2) and (2, 6).
Triangle Q has vertices (−1, −1), (−2, −1) and (−1, −3).
(a) Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle P onto triangle Q. [3]
(b) The area of triangle P is 4 square units. Find the area of triangle Q. [1]
questions.model:
(a) Each vertex of Q is −½ times the corresponding vertex of P, e.g. (2, 2) → (−1, −1) and (4, 2) → (−2, −1).
Enlargement, scale factor −½, centre (0, 0).
(b) Area factor = (−½)² = ¼, so the area of Q = 4 × ¼ = 1 square unit.
questions.tip: If the image is smaller and on the opposite side of the centre (upside down), the scale factor is a negative fraction.

questions.q:
Shape S has vertices (1, 2), (3, 2) and (3, 3).
(a) Reflect shape S in the line y = x. Label the image T and write down its vertices. [2]
(b) Rotate shape T through 90° clockwise about the origin. Label the image U and write down its vertices. [2]
(c) Describe fully the single transformation that maps shape S onto shape U. [2]
ms: (a) B1: two correct vertices of T
(b) B1: two correct vertices of U FT their T
questions.model:
(a) Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates: T = (2, 1), (2, 3), (3, 3).
(b) 90° clockwise about the origin: (x, y) → (y, −x).
U = (1, −2), (3, −2), (3, −3).
(c) S (1, 2) → U (1, −2), (3, 2) → (3, −2), (3, 3) → (3, −3): only the sign of y changes.
Reflection in the x-axis.
questions.tip: A combination of two transformations still needs a single transformation as the answer: 'reflection then rotation' scores 0.

questions.q:
Triangle A has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 4).
Triangle B has vertices (3, 1), (3, −1) and (6, 1).
(a) Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B. [3]
(b) Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle B onto triangle A. [1]
(c) Triangle B is enlarged by scale factor 2, centre (3, 1). Find the coordinates of the vertices of the image. [2]
ms: (b) B1: rotation 90° anticlockwise about (2, 0) FT their (a)
questions.model:
(a) The 3-unit side from (1, 1) up to (1, 4) maps to the side from (3, 1) right to (6, 1), so the turn is 90° clockwise.
The centre is equidistant from each point and its image: (2, 0) works, e.g. (1, 1) is (−1, 1) from (2, 0) and (3, 1) is (1, 1) from (2, 0).
Rotation, 90° clockwise, centre (2, 0).
(b) Rotation, 90° anticlockwise, centre (2, 0).
(c) Relative to (3, 1): (0, 0), (0, −2), (3, 0). Double: (0, 0), (0, −4), (6, 0).
Add the centre back: (3, 1), (3, −3), (9, 1).
questions.tip: Check your centre with every vertex: rotating each one about it must give the image.
